ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown below, four identical containers hold the same number of moles of $H_2O$, $CH_4$, $Ne$, and $He$ at 298 K. If ideal behavior is not assumed, which gas would have the lowest pressure?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The image shows four identical-looking circular containers arranged in a row. They are labeled, from left to right, H2O, CH4, Ne, and He. Reasoning: The problem states that the containers are identical and contain the same number of moles at 298 K, so n, V, and T are held constant. If ideal behavior were assumed, the pressures would be the same. Since ideal behavior is not assumed, real-gas intermolecular attractions matter. Stronger attractive forces reduce the measured pressure because molecules are pulled back from striking the container walls. H2O has the strongest attractions because it is polar and can hydrogen bond. CH4 has only weak dispersion forces, and Ne and He have still weaker dispersion forces. Therefore the gas with the lowest pressure is H2O.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: there are four same-size containers labeled H2O, CH4, Ne, and He. From the text, take that each contains the same number of moles at 298 K, so n, V, and T are held constant. Do not use the ideal gas law alone; compare real-gas attractive forces. The gas with the strongest intermolecular attractions will have the lowest measured pressure because molecules are pulled back from the container walls. Rank attractions: H2O has hydrogen bonding and polarity, CH4 has weak dispersion, Ne and He have still weaker dispersion. Therefore the lowest pressure is for H2O.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the same-size containers are labeled H2O, CH4, Ne, and He. From the text, set n, V, and T equal for all four. Use the van der Waals equation to compare nonideal pressures: the ideal-like term is common except for small b corrections, and the attraction correction -a(n/V)^2 reduces pressure. Compare the gases by their attraction parameter a: water vapor has by far the strongest attractions, so it receives the largest negative pressure correction. Thus H2O would have the lowest pressure.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有四个相同大小、相同形状的圆形容器，从左到右分别标有 H2O、CH4、Ne、He。题干说明四个容器中气体的物质的量相同，温度均为 298 K，因此比较时 n、V、T 相同。
推理：若不假设理想行为，可用 van der Waals 方程比较压力：P = nRT/(V - nb) - a(n/V)^2。在 n、V、T 相同的情况下，理想气体主项基本相同；b 项代表分子体积，会使有效体积减小而略提高压力；a 项代表分子间吸引力，会以 -a(n/V)^2 的形式降低压力。四种气体中，H2O 是强极性分子并能形成氢键，分子间吸引力最强，因此 van der Waals 的 a 参数最大，压力的负修正最大。相较于 CH4、Ne、He，H2O 的实际压力最低。
